meta.title: Vela · The open-source Arc browser alternative
meta.description: Spaces, vertical tabs and the command bar you loved in Arc. Open source, lighter, and still shipping. Free for macOS and Windows.
meta.ogAlt: Vela, the open-source Arc alternative: a browser window with a vertical sidebar of Spaces and tabs.

features.title: The Arc you know, still moving.

spaces.title: Spaces
spaces.body: Work, studio, home. Each Space keeps its own tabs and colour, and can have its own profile, logins and cookies. Swipe between them.

command.title: Command bar
command.body: One field for open tabs, history, the archive and the web, answered in a few milliseconds. Type y then Tab to search YouTube.

split.title: Split view and Peek
split.body: Drop a tab onto another to read them side by side. Links from pinned tabs open in a Peek you can keep or dismiss.

windows.title: Windows that follow you
windows.body: Drag a tab out of the window to give it one of its own, on the same Space, with its own Today.

tidy.title: Tabs that tidy up
tidy.body: Today tabs you stopped using archive themselves after 12 hours, a day, a week or a month. The archive is searchable, so nothing is lost.

features.more: Also built in: Boosts, Air Traffic Control, Little windows, reader mode, picture in picture, a content blocker, a password manager and rebindable shortcuts.

import.title: Bring your whole Arc with you.
import.lead: On first launch Vela offers to import everything. Run it again later and it merges instead of duplicating.
items: Spaces, with their names, emoji and colours
Profiles attached to the same Spaces
Passwords and cookies, so you stay logged in
Your Chrome Web Store extensions, reinstalled in one click
import.other: Coming from Chrome, Brave, Edge, Safari or Firefox? Those imports are there too.

extensions.title: Your extensions come too.
extensions.lead: Install them straight from the Chrome Web Store. 16 of the 20 most used work today.

open.title: Nobody can freeze it.
open.lead: Vela is GPL-3.0 and built in the open. Every version, and every fork, stays open source.

privacy.title: No account. No telemetry.
privacy.body: Crash reports stay on your disk. Passwords live in your system keychain. Safe Browsing is checked on your machine.

fresh.title: A fresh Chromium, on its own.
fresh.body: A bot checks for a new engine every 6 hours, runs the whole test suite and ships the release.

yours.title: Yours to read and change.
yours.body: TypeScript and Electron, every decision written down, end-to-end tests on macOS and Windows. Issues and pull requests welcome.

items.a: Not dead, frozen. The Browser Company stopped building new Arc features in May 2025 to focus on Dia. Arc still gets Chromium security patches. If you are happy with Arc as it is, keep it. Vela is for when you want it to keep moving.

items.q: Is Vela a fork of Arc?
items.a: No. Arc is closed source, so there is nothing to fork. Vela is written from scratch and borrows ideas, not code, names or assets.
Yes, and it will stay that way. Vela is GPL-3.0: no subscription, no account, no paid tier.

Install them from the Chrome Web Store. Of the 20 most used, 16 work fully or with minor glitches, each tested by hand. Ad blockers rely on an API Electron lacks, so Vela's built-in blocker does that job.
No telemetry and no account. Crash dumps stay on your disk. The only call home is the update check, made to GitHub Releases.

Engine updates are automated: a check every 6 hours, the full test suite, then a release. Features ship in regular releases. And because it is GPL-3.0, Vela does not depend on any one person or company.

final.title: Set sail.
final.lead: Free, open source, and yours. Download Vela and bring your Spaces with you.
